name: Leek
grown_as: The garden leek, a biennial grown as an annual for its long white shank, lifted from autumn through to spring. William has 'Musselburgh' (broad, mid to dark green leaves) and 'Blue Green Autumn Neptune' (blue-green leaves). Drawn with blue-green leaves. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: Year 1: a single upright stem-like shank of tightly wrapped leaf bases, 15 to 30 cm long and 2 to 5 cm thick, with flat leaves fanning out from its top to 40 to 60 cm. No true bulb. Year 2: one stout, solid, round flower stem 1 to 1.5 m with a large round head.

leaf.arrangement: In two opposite ranks, so the leaves fan out flat in one plane like a hand of cards
leaf.outline: Long, flat strap, 30 to 60 cm by 2 to 5 cm, parallel-sided
leaf.base: A long sheath wrapping the shank, white below where it was in the dark
leaf.tip: Narrowing to a blunt point; tips often arch over and droop
leaf.veins: Many fine parallel veins along the leaf
leaf.surface: Folded in a V along a keel (solid, NOT hollow), smooth, with a waxy bloom
leaf.stalk: None: the sheaths make the shank
leaf.colour: Blue-green to dark grey-green; the shank white, turning pale green where the leaves part

flower.form: A large round ball of many small cup-shaped flowers
flower.petals: Six tepals, free, oval, pointed, held in a cup
flower.colour: Pale pink to lilac or white, the midvein sometimes darker
flower.centre: Six stamens with yellow-purple anthers sticking out beyond the tepals
flower.behind: A papery spathe with a long tapering beak, wrapping the whole head in bud, splitting and falling as it opens
flower.carried: Hundreds of flowers on long thin stalks from one point, forming a dense round umbel at the top of a tall stem, held upright
flower.size: Flowers 4 to 6 mm; heads 7 to 10 cm across
flower.season: June to August of the second year

fruit: The head dries to a straw-brown ball of papery three-lobed capsules that split to show black angular seeds. Some heads carry small bulbils among the flowers.
seedling: A single thin grass-like seed leaf, first bent double like a hairpin with the black seed case on one end (the 'crook'), then straightening; then thin flat true leaves, two-ranked from the start.
winter: Hardy: stands in the ground all winter, the outer leaves yellowing and the tips flopping, the shank lifted as needed.

leaf: a long flat strap folded in a V along a keel, solid not hollow
a white sheath at the base
bloom: a round dense ball of many small cup-shaped pale lilac-pink flowers
a papery beaked spathe falling from below
seed: a black, angular, wrinkled seed, about 3 mm
seedling: one thin grass-like seed leaf bent like a hairpin with the black seed case on its tip
young: a thin upright shank with flat leaves fanned out in one plane
crop: a long thick white shank with no bulb, a little swollen at the base
flat blue-green leaves fanned out in one plane from its top
a mass of white roots from a flat base
flower: one tall, stout, solid, round stem
a large round pale lilac head on top
seedhead: a dry straw-brown round head of papery capsules

look_alikes: Wild leek and the Bristol onion (Allium sphaerocephalon) have small heads and thin leaves. Onion has hollow round leaves and a bulb. Garlic leaves are flat but narrower and also two-ranked, and garlic makes a bulb of cloves. Elephant garlic is the same species, grown for its large cloves.
